text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a spike in GPU job failures in eu-west-1. Lots of `rdma` handshake timeouts and high per-token latency. Autoscaler spun up +12 nodes in the last 20m, cost alert firing. Anyone touching netpols?

trevor: Not me. What errors are you seeing exactly?

maya: Example from worker logs: `ibv_rc_pingpong: connect error: -110 (Connection timed out)` and then k8s reports `CrashLoopBackOff` on certain p2 pods. Also kube-proxy logs show a lot of connection resets.

sasha: Could be east-west blocked. Do we have a recent NetPolicy change? I saw an egress-hardening PR merged last night targeting namespace `ml-training`. @liam any clue?

liam: Yeah that PR added a default-deny egress for `ml-training` with an allowlist for specific services. It might be missing CNI/encapsulation CIDRs.

maya: That would explain it — RDMA and VXLAN rely on host-level encapsulation between nodes, not just pod-to-pod on 10.0.0.0/16. When those egress rules only allow pod CIDRs, VXLAN/underlay traffic can be blocked.

trevor: Can you paste the netpol?

maya: Sure:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-ml-training
  namespace: ml-training
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
```

maya: No VXLAN/encap CIDRs or host CIDRs allowed.

sasha: Oof. That will block kube-node to kube-node VXLAN encapsulation (usually something like 192.168.0.0/16) and also blocks IP-in-IP for some CNIs.

ops-bot: @channel cost-alert: infra.ec2.eu-west-1 spike > 18% over baseline in last 30m.

liam: Quick mitigation: add rule allowing the node CIDR and the CNI encapsulation range, and allow UDP/8472 (if flannel) or protocol 50 for GRE etc depending on CNI.

trevor: Also check MTU fragmentation. If netpol allowed only small packets it could cause ICMP fragmentation issues for RDMA. Run `iperf3` between nodes and look for PMTU blackhole symptoms.

maya: I spun a netshoot pod and ran tcpdump on the host interface. See this capture showing VXLAN frames dropped at source after netpol enforcement: `vni 4096, proto 0x6558` and then `ICMP frag needed, mtu=1420`.

sasha: That's consistent — our node overlay MTU is 1450, but some pods using SR-IOV expect 9000. NetPolicy egress that only allows 10.0.0.0/16 will prevent the DF/ICMP replies making it worse.

liam: Proposed quick patch (apply to `ml-training`):

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-node-and-encap
  namespace: ml-training
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 192.168.0.0/16
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 172.16.0.0/12
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
    - protocol: UDP
```

maya: Applying that now to unblock traffic, will monitor.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: networkpolicy/allow-node-and-encap created by liam in ml-training

maya: After the patch, RDMA handshakes recover for ~80% of pods, autoscaler stopped adding nodes. Job failure rate down to normal.

trevor: Follow-up items: add test in pre-merge CI that runs a traceflow/ephemeral pod to validate netpols don't block node-to-node encapsulation; document expected CNI encapsulation ranges for each region; and run a cost postmortem on the autoscaler surge.

sasha: I'll own the CI check. maya can you open the cost ticket with the spike numbers?

maya: Will do — opening ticket now and adding logs + pcap. Thanks all :thumbsup:

liam: Also ping security to make sure allowlist is explicit instead of broadening forever. We should keep least privilege but allow necessary host ranges.

maya: Noted. Closing thread once ticket is up.
